items.problem: The migration analyzer under-detects the in-process/legacy background-task family, so files that drive background activation without literally naming IBackgroundTask/BackgroundTaskBuilder get no background-tasks TODO routing.
items.evidence: unsupported-api-inventory.json line 20 matches only '\bIBackgroundTask\b|BackgroundTaskBuilder'. The migrated SampleConfiguration.cs uses BackgroundExecutionManager.RequestAccessAsync(), BackgroundTaskRegistrationGroup, SystemTrigger; App.xaml.cs used group.BackgroundActivated; original App overrode OnBackgroundActivated (session-log.txt lines 294, 304-305).
items.root_cause: The detection pattern is keyed to two tokens and misses the rest of the Windows.ApplicationModel.Background surface + the Application.OnBackgroundActivated activation hook.
items.proposed_fix: Broaden the adaptable entry's regex to also match BackgroundExecutionManager, BackgroundTaskRegistrationGroup, SystemTrigger, TimeTrigger, ApplicationTrigger, MaintenanceTrigger and OnBackgroundActivated so any file touching the in-process background model is routed to the background-tasks anchor.
items.generalizes: Every UWP background-activation sample/app uses this family; keying detection to only two tokens systematically misses the single-process/in-process pattern that is the common case, so the agent gets no guidance on those files.
